Team —

Escalating OrbitCloud's request for an AWS private offer. They've asked for the following non-standard terms (see attached SOW and initial draft PO):
- 30% off published list pricing for a 24-month commitment (~$600k ARR).
- Marketplace rev-share carveout: OrbitCloud requests AWS commission be limited so they net ~12% (effectively asking for a rev-share concession).
- Net 45 payment terms and a reseller clause to allow OrbitCloud to bundle/redistribute to their customers.

Why this matters: OrbitCloud is a strategic EMEA-US hybrid customer with multiple product integrations; closing on these terms will accelerate a broader platform partnership and potential marketplace co-marketing. Procurement needs a private offer by Nov 20.

Risks / considerations:
- Revenue economics: 30% off + rev-share carveout materially reduces unit economics; we should model NRR/COGS impacts.
- Marketplace policy: AWS typically requires partner rev-share alignment; exceptions are rare and often need partner/program teams to approve.
- Legal: reseller clause could expose us to downstream compliance and data processing complexities.

Suggested response (what I think we can push for):
1) Counter to 22% off list (instead of 30%) for 24-month commit with a minimum annual spend of $300k per year.
2) Rev-share: offer a 10% rev-share to OrbitCloud (not 12%), but structured so Redwood remains compliant with AWS fee flows — propose a separate rebate rather than altering the AWS listing.
3) Payment: Net 45 for initial year, then move to Net 30 on renewal.
4) Reseller: allow limited reseller rights with a tied indemnity clause and regular audits; legal to draft.

Please reply with approvals/edits — procurement is pushing on timeline (Nov 20). I can loop in PM/Field engineers for any SSO/networking concerns if this moves forward.

Attachments: OrbitCloud_SOW_v3.pdf, AWS_Private_Offer_Draft.docx, revshare_calc.xlsx

Diego

Redwood Inference
